body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

أما بعد فإن الله تعالى افترض الصيام على عباده وبين حكمة افتراضه فقال تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون أياما معدودات فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر فعدة من أيام أخر وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين فمن تطوع خيرا فهو خير له وأن تصوموا خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن هدى للناس وبينات من الهدى والفرقان
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon the one who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his practice until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: God, exalted, made fasting (ṣawm) obligatory upon His servants and set out the wisdom in His making it obligatory. He said, exalted: {O you who believe, fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you may become God-conscious — for a fixed number of days. Whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then a number of other days; and upon those who are able to do it there is a compensatory payment, the feeding of a poor person. Whoever volunteers good, it is better for him; and that you fast is better for you, if only you knew. The month of Ramadan, in which the Qur'an was sent down as guidance for people, and as clear signs of guidance and of the criterion

flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY, AND A TRUNCATED SCRIPTURE QUOTATION — STYLE GUIDE §9 AND §11. The page breaks off in the middle of Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:185, immediately after wa-bayyinātin min al-hudā wa-l-furqān. The opening curly brace of the quotation is therefore never closed in the source and is not closed here. The verse has NOT been restored from memory. This is also §10 territory: the excerpt is the title's promise of 'the rulings of fasting' with not one ruling yet given, the whole substance being in the .docx download.

flags.arabic: وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين
options: upon those who are able to do it there is a compensatory payment (fidyah), the feeding of a poor person
upon those who can only bear it with hardship there is a ransom
those who find it burdensome must feed a poor person
flags.note: This clause is one of the most heavily disputed in the verse — whether yuṭīqūnahu means 'are able to' or 'can manage it only with difficulty' decides who the dispensation applies to, and the schools divide on it. The Sheikh quotes the verse and the page stops before he says anything about it. The English renders the Arabic as it stands, without adopting an interpretation, and the reader is not told which way he goes, because the source does not say.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-21 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer or delivered the lecture. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The opening is the khuṭbat al-ḥājah, the standard formula with which the Sheikh begins a lecture. It is rendered in full rather than abbreviated, since it is part of the text as published.

EXCERPT ONLY. The page publishes the opening of the lecture and breaks off; the full text sits behind the .docx download recorded in source_download_link. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and the thought has not been completed. The site must render this with an excerpt banner and never as a whole article.

The quotation runs from Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:183 to the middle of 2:185. The reference is not given in the source; it has been identified but no part of the text has been supplied beyond where the source stops.
'Compensatory payment' for fidyah and 'God-conscious' for the verbal sense of taqwā follow the glossary.
